title: Corner-to-corner triangle shawl
subtitle: A diagonal-build two-colour triangle in DK on a 4 mm hook, using the C2C dc-in-corner-space method
excerpt: Corner-to-corner crochet builds a triangle by adding one block-square per row on the increase side, then decreasing one block per row on the other. Each block is a small square of three trebles worked into a chain-2 corner space. This shawl grows from a single corner block to a long side of 130 cm, then decreases back to a single block. Two DK colours work in stripes to emphasise the diagonal geometry.
sourceNotes: Corner-to-corner crochet construction synthesised from established fibre arts techniques. The C2C method with ch-2 corner spaces and 3-treble blocks is a widely documented technique with no single original source.
heroPrompt: A triangular crochet shawl in teal and cream DK yarn pinned flat on a blocking mat, showing the diagonal grid of corner-to-corner blocks clearly from above.

crochet.gaugeText: Each C2C block measures 2.5 x 2.5 cm with DK yarn on a 4 mm hook. 4 blocks = 10 cm.
crochet.finishedSizeText: Approximately 130 cm along each long side (the two equal sides of the triangle), blocked.

glossaryTerms.definition: The repeating unit in corner-to-corner crochet: ch 6, then 3 tr into the 4th, 5th, and 6th chains from the hook, forming a small square with a ch-2 corner space in one corner.
The ch-2 space at the corner of each C2C block. On subsequent rows the next block's 3 trebles are worked into this space rather than into the chains.

content.text: Corner-to-corner crochet builds from one corner of a triangle outward. Every row on the increase half adds one new
C2C block
at the diagonal edge. Each block is anchored to the
corner space

of the block in the row below. Once the triangle reaches its widest point (52 blocks across the hypotenuse), the decrease half removes one block at the start of each row until one block remains. The shawl uses two DK colours alternated in two-row stripes to show the diagonal geometry. You carry the unused colour up the edge on alternate rows.

The finished long sides measure 130 cm each at gauge, with each block 2.5 cm square (4 blocks per 10 cm). The hypotenuse at the widest point spans 52 blocks diagonally. Tension matters: a block that runs larger than 2.5 cm will produce a longer shawl; one that runs smaller will produce a shorter one. Measure after the first 10 blocks on your increase triangle.

attrs.title: Materials
attrs.body: Colour A: approximately 200 g DK-weight yarn. Colour B: approximately 200 g DK-weight yarn. A 4 mm hook (US G/6). Tapestry needle. Craft scissors. Stitch markers. Blocking mat and pins. Tape measure.

content.text: Gauge

Each C2C block measures 2.5 x 2.5 cm with DK yarn on a 4 mm hook. Work the first 4 rows of the triangle (10 blocks total) and measure: 4 blocks should span 10 cm both horizontally and vertically. If your blocks run larger, drop a hook size; if smaller, go up a hook size.
Stitches used
ch: chain -- UK and US shared.
sl st: slip stitch -- UK and US shared.
tr: treble (UK) -- the same move as US "double crochet" (dc). Yarn over twice, insert hook, draw up loop, (yarn over, draw through 2 loops) three times.
dc: double crochet (UK) -- used at the join point between blocks on decrease rows.
Pattern

The triangle works in two halves: an increase half (rows 1 to 52) where each row gains one block at the right diagonal edge, and a decrease half (rows 53 to 103) where each row loses one block at the same edge. Colour changes happen at the start of every right-side row: row 1 colour A, row 3 colour B, row 5 colour A, and so on in two-row stripes.
First block (row 1)
Using colour A, ch 6. 3 tr in 4th ch from hook (the 3 skipped chains form the corner space). Turn. (1 block)
Row 2 (increase, colour A continues)
Ch 6. 3 tr in 4th ch from hook (new block at edge). Ch 3. Sl st in corner space of previous block. Ch 3. 3 tr in same corner space. Turn. (2 blocks)
Rows 3 to 52 (increase half, colour stripes)

Change to colour B at the start of row 3. On every increase row: ch 6, 3 tr in 4th ch from hook to add the new edge block; then work across the existing blocks by sl st into the top of the previous row's edge block, ch 3, 3 tr in each corner space along the row; end with 3 tr in the last corner space of the previous row. Change colour every 2 rows throughout. At the end of row 52 you have 52 blocks across the diagonal. (52 blocks)
Row 53 (first decrease row)

Turn the work. Sl st across the top 3 tr of the first block and into the corner space (this slips past the edge block without adding a new one). Ch 3. 3 tr in same corner space. Continue working a block in each remaining corner space across. Turn. (51 blocks)
Rows 54 to 103 (decrease half)

Continue repeating the decrease row method: sl st across the first block into the corner space at the start of each row, then work one block in every remaining corner space across. Maintain the two-row colour stripe throughout. The block count reduces by one per row. At the end of row 103 you have 1 block. Fasten off.
Finishing

Weave in all ends securely on the wrong side. Wet-block by soaking the finished triangle in cool water for 10 minutes, gently pressing water out in a clean towel, then pinning the two long sides and the hypotenuse to the stated dimensions on a blocking mat. Pin each corner first, then pin the edges at 10 cm intervals.
Care
Handwash in cool water with mild soap. Do not tumble-dry. Lay flat on a clean towel and ease to shape while damp.
What to try next

Once you are confident with the C2C block rhythm, a C2C rectangle blanket uses the same method but turns the increase at a specific row count instead of working a full triangle. Three or more colours in single-row stripes produce a more intricate striped effect. Working the same block construction in aran weight on a 5 mm hook produces a coarser, heavier throw.
